persona.who: 22, Indo-Canadian, came out to her Punjabi parents last year, they went silent, now talk only about weather. She still goes home for Diwali.
persona.note: since I told my parents about my girlfriend they haven't said one real thing to me. we talk about the weather. I still go home for diwali and sit at the table and it's like I'm a guest

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being treated as a guest in your own home to standing in your own truth at that table.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being treated as a stranger, and the quiet anger of it, named without blame.

understanding.core_struggle: My parents' expectations weigh on me
understanding.mirror: You go home for Diwali and sit at the table, and it is like being a guest in your own house.
understanding.insight: The silence is not a mystery to solve. It is a wall they built, and you are standing on the wrong side of it, wondering why the door is closed.

queries.hook: Being treated as a stranger in your own home, and the quiet anger of watching the bond you had become a performance.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A son who was sent away by his own father, yet stood in his truth and was proven right by the one who had to come back to him.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

matched.label: My parents' expectations weigh on me

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is frozen, caught between two armies of family and duty. Krishna tells him that it is better to follow the path that is truly yours, even if you stumble, than to perform someone else's role with perfection. The idea is that your own nature holds a truth that fits you alone. When you act from that honest fit, you carry no wrong.
verse.for_you: You are still going home for Diwali, sitting at your own table, but the silence tells you they are asking you to perform a role that is not yours. Let your own truth be the offering at the table today, even if it feels imperfect.

verse.speaker: Tulsidas
verse.setting: Ravana's ministers flatter him as Ram's army arrives; the poet comments.
verse.sanskrit: सचिव बैद गुर तीनि जौं प्रिय बोलहिं भय आस राज धर्म तन तीनि कर होइ बेगिहीं नास ॥
verse.line: When advisers, doctors and teachers only say what pleases you, the ruin comes quickly.
verse.translation: When a minister, a doctor and a teacher speak only to please, out of fear or hope of reward, then the kingdom, the body and righteousness are soon destroyed.
verse.why: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.

prasang.title: Mandodari pleads, the ministers flatter
prasang.summary: Mandodari takes Ravana aside and begs him to return Sita before it is too late. He laughs at her fear and goes to court, where his ministers tell him only what pleases him. Tulsidas notes that when advisers, doctors and teachers speak only to please, ruin comes quickly.
prasang.story_hook: Mandodari took her husband's hand and led him somewhere the ministers couldn't hear.
prasang.lesson: Beware a circle that only tells you what you want to hear.

verse.meaning: Ravana sits in his court as Ram's army waits outside. His ministers flatter him, telling him what he wants to hear because they are afraid of him. Tulsidas steps in and says that when the people around you only speak to please you, ruin follows fast. He is warning anyone who is surrounded by yes-men, whether in a kingdom or in a family.
verse.for_you: You are in a house where the people around you have chosen silence over truth. They are not telling you what is hard because it is easier to talk about the weather. Notice this pattern. They are protecting their comfort, not your place.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying on the ground after losing his kingdom. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt, not to settle for little, and to stop fearing. She says to set his mind on what is truly good and pull himself together. The point is that past failure does not define a person. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: Your parents' silence is a heavy thing. But their coldness does not have to shrink your sense of who you are. Hold onto your own truth, even when the room feels empty.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi turns to Yudhishthira in the forest. She sees him waiting on fate and tells him that looking down on himself will not feed them. She says nothing good grows from self-contempt. The idea is that you could act with your full mind on a good goal, and stop fearing the outcome. It is a call to keep working as if your effort is the only thing that matters.
verse.for_you: Your parents have made you feel small, but that is their choice, not your truth. You still carry your own mind and your own work. Let your effort be the proof of who you are, and do not let their silence shrink your view of yourself.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha how a free person moves through the world. He says to do the work in front of you, speak gently, and read people’s hearts, and you will not sink in the world. A person who is free from wanting and not-wanting, who sees friend and foe alike, treats the whole world as family. They neither grieve nor crave, because they are busy outside and calm inside.
verse.for_you: Your parents have built a wall, and you are standing on the wrong side, wondering why the door is closed. Do not look down on yourself for their silence. You are not the problem here. Do your work for today, speak gently if they speak, and keep your heart steady.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna is on giving, effort, food, and speech, telling Arjuna about three kinds of each. He says speech that is true, kind, and helpful is the right way to talk. It does not mean hiding the hard parts. It means saying them without cruelty. It is a way to hold your ground without breaking the room.
verse.for_you: At home, the talk is only about the weather. You can speak the truth about how you feel, but you could do it without cruelty. You could not wound them, but you could not hide who you are either. Speak kindly, but speak truly.

story.title: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
story.story_hook: He told his brother the truth in front of the whole court, and his brother kicked him.
story.summary: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
story.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

anchor.speaker: Vibhishan
anchor.setting: Vibhishan, Ravana's younger brother, advises him in open court.
anchor.sanskrit: चौदह भुवन एक पति होई। भूत द्रोह तिष्टइ नहिं सोई॥ गुन सागर नागर नर जोऊ। अलप लोभ भल कहइ न कोऊ ॥
anchor.line: You may be gifted and clever, but even a little greed and people stop calling you good.
anchor.translation: Even a sole master of the fourteen worlds cannot last if he makes enemies of living beings. A person may be an ocean of virtues and clever too, but if he has even a little greed, no one calls him good.
anchor.why: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

prasang.title: Vibhishan speaks up and is kicked
prasang.summary: Vibhishan, bowing to his brother, advises him to return Sita: good sense and bad sense live in every heart, and Ravana is feeding the wrong one. Ravana kicks him. Vibhishan still says Ravana is like a father to him, and then he leaves, telling him not to blame him.
prasang.story_hook: He told his brother the truth in front of the whole court, and his brother kicked him.
prasang.lesson: Say the hard thing with respect; if you are struck for it, you may go.

story.hook_title: Vibhishan told Ravana the truth in front of the court, and Ravana kicked him
story.teaser: Vibhishan told Ravana the truth in front of the court, and Ravana kicked him
story.for_you: The silence at your table is Ravana's court. You do not need to kick the table to be seen. Speak the weather, then speak the truth. If they still turn away, you know your own worth.

script: You are carrying the weight of a silence that treats you like a stranger. Your parents, your family, they have gone quiet since they learned about your girlfriend, and now every conversation is just the weather. You are still going home for Diwali, but you are sitting at your own table feeling like a guest.

Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield. Arjuna is frozen between two armies of his own family. He does not know what to do, caught between who he is and what the world demands. And Krishna replies:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

Krishna says it is better to walk your own path, even if you stumble, than to play someone else's role perfectly. This is not about the caste you were born into or the family script they wrote for you. It is about finding the honest work that fits your own nature, and doing it as an offering. When you act from that true fit, you carry no wrong.

When you sit at that table for Diwali today, let your own truth be the offering. You do not have to perform the role they expect. Just be there, exactly as you are, with your own path imperfectly walked.
What offering can you place on the table today?

depth.life: You are back at the table for Diwali. The food is familiar but the air is not. Your parents speak about the rain. You are the guest they made you, and the weight of their expectations is heavier than the feast.
depth.points: The truth here is that you are not failing because you are imperfect. You are failing only if you try to wear a life that was never yours to begin with.
depth.practice: Before you sit down at the table, name one small thing you genuinely care about today. Let that be your only offering.
depth.question: What is one small truth you can offer at the table today?
